title: Adaptive pricing and clarity playpad
content:
Context:

Quick scratchpad for a customer-facing feature: let app owners expose explicit cost vs clarity controls to end users, plus developer hooks for programmatic defaults. Aim: reduce surprise bills, surface predictable quality tradeoffs, increase adoption in price-sensitive segments (marketplaces, consumer apps).

Problem statements:
- Users/devs today either pay-per-token blindly or rely on opaque model choices; hard to explain tradeoffs to end users.
- Apps want deterministic unit economics for features (e.g., chat summaries vs high-fidelity drafting).
- Current platform controls (batching, quantization, model variants) are powerful but low-level for app teams.

Core idea (high-level):
Provide a first-class "clarity tier" abstraction that maps to a set of runtime knobs and a pricing ladder. Developer can expose a simple slider/presets to end users or set per-route defaults. Backend maps tiers to: model variant, max tokens, sampling temp/top-k, quantization profile, batching priority, and a per-token price multiplier.

Key components:
1) Clarity tiers (examples):
   - economy (fast, cheapest): low token budgets, aggressive quantization, deterministic decode (greedy/low temp), lower sampling quality
   - balanced (default): standard model variant, default budget and temp
   - premium (high-fidelity): best model variant, higher token allowance, higher temperature, optionally run >=1 refinement pass

2) Developer API surface:
   - request param: clarity_tier: [economy|balanced|premium|custom] (string)
   - custom: allow explicit override for each knob (max_tokens, temp, model_hint, quant_profile) for devs who want fine control
   - server-side defaults in project/route config with UI labels, price per tier, and opt-in E2E telemetry

3) Billing mapping:
   - base per-token price anchored to model family + tier multiplier (e.g., premium x1.6, economy x0.6)
   - per-response fixed surcharge for premium (when doing extra passes or reranking)
   - credits/allowances: optional monthly credits for certain tiers for trial users

4) UX primitives (for clients):
   - Preset cards with one-line benefit and estimated cost per 1k chars (UI shows estimate computed by tokens * multiplier)
   - Inline clarity indicator next to responses (cheap|balanced|premium), tooltip shows what changed (e.g., model: redwood-v2-medium -> redwood-v2-large, temp: 0.2 -> 0.7)
   - Developer console: controls to tune mapping and preview quality vs estimated price for sample prompts

User stories (candidate):
- As a consumer user, I want to pick a cheaper mode when I only need quick snippets so I don't blow through my credits.
- As a product manager, I want to force certain routes to premium so high-value flows always get high quality.
- As an engineer, I want a single API field I can toggle per request rather than composing multiple runtime knobs.
- As finance, I want per-tier usage breakdown, median tokens per response, and net unit cost so we can model revenue impact.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- API accepts clarity_tier param and respects mapping to model and max_tokens for host accounts
- Console shows per-tier pricing multipliers and a sample-prompt quality preview for each tier
- Billing pipeline tags usage by tier for reporting; able to run queries like "sum(cost) by clarity_tier last 30d"
- Developer docs + quickstart snippet and two client SDK helpers (js+py) demonstrating toggling tier

Metrics to track:
- percent of requests using non-default tier (adoption)
- median tokens and latency per tier
- cost delta vs baseline per route (expected vs actual)
- customer-reported satisfaction (NPS/CSAT) for flows with tier selector

Experiments / rollout plan:
- Internal canary: enable in a single internal org to gather telemetry and compare quality metrics on same prompts across tiers (A/B by request)
- Beta partners: 3 external customers in consumer verticals with opt-in toggles in their dev console; collect UX feedback on preset wording and estimated cost clarity
- Full GA: pricing docs + recommended defaults + dashboards

Open questions / risks:
- Will simple multiplier-based pricing misalign with actual infra cost if premium routes trigger extra CPU/GPU work? (Need cost model linking runtime config to infra cost)
- How to present "estimated cost" in UI when batching & caching change final token billing? (Provide range and percentile estimate; show final cost in receipt)
- Regulatory / compliance: premium might use less quantization (i.e., less lossy). Any privacy implications? (document mappings for SOC/ISO audits)

Implementation sketch (runtime mapping):
- mapping table: clarity_tier -> {model_variant, quant_profile, max_tokens, temp, batch_priority, postprocess_passes}
- router resolves model_variant, picks runtime pool, sets billing tags
- caching layer key includes clarity_tier so economy/premium responses don't accidentally reuse incompatible cached completions

Telemetry (events):
- clarity_choice_set (user_id?, session_id?, route, clarity_tier, client_sdk)
- clarity_result (request_id, clarity_tier, model_variant, tokens_in/out, latency_ms, price_estimate, price_charged)

Docs + developer snippets (quick):
JS (pseudo):
const resp = await redwood.generate({ prompt, clarity_tier: 'economy' })

Console mock copy suggestions:
- Economy — Faster & cheaper for quick ideas
- Balanced — Good default, balanced price vs quality
- Premium — Highest quality for drafting and complex reasoning

Notes / next steps (today):
- Sync with runtime team to validate cost multipliers for mapping table (estimate infra delta for premium vs balanced)
- Draft a shallow UX prototype (2 cards + inline tooltip) for design review
- Create an analytics SQL query template to compute cost delta by tier (for billing)**

Random brainlets / tangents:
- Could tie clarity tiers to a "confidence score" computed by a cheap classifier to recommend premium only when model confidence below threshold
- Consider per-domain or per-route tier overrides (e.g., payments flow pinned to premium)
- Maybe add an "auto-scale to premium for X tokens of user intent" experiment where the system upgrades mid-response when complexity predicted

Bottom line: this is a low-friction abstraction that surfaces cost/quality to end users and developers with a single API knob and corresponding billing visibility. MVP should prioritize predictable billing and simple mappings; followups can introduce dynamic upgrades and confidence-based recommendations.
